## Context / Problem

Discovered from obtuse-phenocryst-verdin. `run_git` in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` (the `subprocess.run` call at line 199 and the `subprocess.Popen` in `_run_in_group` at line 229) runs git with `text=True` and no `encoding`, and `ssh_keygen_version` in `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:58` runs `ssh -V` the same way. Python then decodes the output with the locale codec. On Windows that is cp1252, so non-ASCII git output (commit subjects, paths, ticket titles) is garbled, or raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on the bytes cp1252 leaves undefined (0x81/0x8D/0x8F/0x90/0x9D). Every tickets-store git read goes through `run_git`, so this affects Windows users of the tracker, not only tests.

Reproduced on macOS at origin/main `1654f3e3e53`: under `python -X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning`, `gitutil.run_git(None, "--version")`, `gitutil.run_git(None, "--version", timeout=5)` and `sshsig.ssh_keygen_version()` each raise `EncodingWarning: 'encoding' argument not specified`.

## Approach

Name the codec at each call site, so decoding no longer depends on the host locale:

- `run_git` and `_run_in_group`: pass `encoding="utf-8" if text else None`. git emits UTF-8 by default (`i18n.logOutputEncoding` defaults to UTF-8), so UTF-8 is the right codec. The conditional is required: `subprocess` switches to text mode whenever `encoding` is set, so passing it unconditionally would break the `text=False` binary-stdin contract documented in `run_git`'s docstring (gitutil.py:177-181). Decoding stays strict, matching what POSIX hosts with a UTF-8 locale do today.
- `ssh_keygen_version`: pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`. The output is a version banner that is only matched by `_VERSION_RE`, so a stray undecodable byte must not crash the probe.

This adds no config key, env var or flag. It is portable: an explicit codec is the platform-neutral form. It removes the only platform-dependent input (the locale) and uses no POSIX-only API.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`: `run_git` and `_run_in_group` pass the encoding.
- `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`: `ssh_keygen_version` passes the encoding.
- `tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py` (new): regression tests.

## Testing

`tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py` runs each call in a child interpreter started with `-X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning`, and asserts that the child exits 0. Cases:
- `run_git(<tmp repo>, "log", "-1", "--format=%s")` without a timeout returns the non-ASCII subject `"café ✓"` intact;
- the same call with `timeout=30` (the `_run_in_group` path) returns the same subject;
- `run_git(..., text=False)` still returns `bytes` (edge case: binary mode stays binary);
- `ssh_keygen_version()` completes without the warning (skipped when `ssh` is not on PATH, because the `FileNotFoundError` path never decodes).

Each of the first, second and fourth cases fails on the pre-fix code, with the child exiting non-zero because of the `EncodingWarning`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `run_git`, `_run_in_group` and `ssh_keygen_version` each name their encoding. Check: `pytest tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py` passes, and the same tests fail when run against `src/` at origin/main `1654f3e3e53`.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
